Long, long ago, there lived a kind old man named Noah. Among all the people in the world, he alone remembered to be good and always listened to his heart.
One day, God said to Noah: "A great flood is coming. Build a big boat called an ark, and keep your family and the animals safe."
Noah believed, and he got to work. For many days, he and his sons built a great big wooden ark.
And so the animals made their way to the ark — two by two, big and small. Elephants and rabbits, lions and birds all walked along, one after another.
Noah gently guided each animal across the little bridge and into the ark. Every single one found a warm and cozy place inside.
Noah and his family were the last to step inside the ark. The great door closed quietly, and a peaceful stillness came over everyone.
And then the rain began to fall from the sky. It poured harder and harder, day and night, and the water rose higher and higher.
Soon the water covered all the land. Only the ark floated quietly on the waves, rocking gently like a giant cradle.
Inside, it was warm and cozy. Noah fed the animals, petted them, and took good care of every single one.
Many days went by. At last the rain stopped, and the sun peeked through the little window of the ark.
Noah sent a white dove out of the window to find out if the land had appeared. But the dove came back — there was still no land to be seen.
A few days later, the dove came back again — and in its beak it carried a little green branch! That meant that somewhere, land had already appeared.
The water began to go down, and the ark gently came to rest on top of a mountain. The land was coming back.
Noah opened the door, and everyone stepped out onto the fresh green earth. The animals scattered across the hills, overjoyed to be free.
Then a great rainbow appeared in the sky. It was a sign of a wonderful promise: there would never be such a great flood again.
And so a wonderful new world began. Noah, his family, and all the animals were happy to be alive again on the beautiful earth.
